newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Petron seeks August reformate in a tender.
newsitem.headline: Petron seeks August reformate in a tender.

text.p: Philippines oil refiner Petron Corp has re-emerged for its gasoline requirements but in a tender to selected sellers, traders said on Wednesday.
Petron is seeking 100,000 barrels of 95 or 97-octane unleaded reformate for delivery August 10-20 on a cost-and-freight basis to Bataan.
The tender closed on July 28 but results have yet to be announced, a trader said.
Early last week, Petron cancelled its first gasoline import tender in about two years, because of "operational considerations", a company official said.
The cancelled tender which sought 70,000 barrels of 95-octane unleaded gasoline for August 11-15 delivery, closed on July 18 and was vaild for the day.

Since the cancellation, European major British Petroleum has sold around 100,000 barrels of August delivery 97-octane unleaded gasoline to Petron, through negotiations, at around 60-80 cents per barrel over Singapore 97-octane quotes.

Petron, which operates a 155,000-bpd refinery in Bataan, north of the capital Manila, had not issued an gasoline import tender since 1995 but had to re-emerge to buy due to increased domestic demand, an official had said.
But industry sources had also said the import requirement was also partly due to the unexpected shutdown of a 15,000-barrel-per-day (bpd) thermal cracker on June 20 following an explosion.
The unit, which produces diesel, gasoline and liquefied petroleum gas, is expected to restart mid-August.
Petron also plans a maintenance shutdown of a 85,000-bpd crude distillation unit (CDU) No.2 and 17,000-bpd reformer September 1-12.
